chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the marwa (a type of wood/strap), the qasabah (reed/stalk), and the wood; are animals slaughtered with them if they do not find a knife? He said: 'If they cut the windpipe (throat), there is no objection to that.'

key_terms.الْأَوْدَاج: The windpipe and veins in the throat
key_terms.الْقَصَبَة: Reed or stalk used for slaughter
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: A type of wood or strap used for slaughter

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for valid slaughter using non-knife items like wood or reeds in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the criterion for valid slaughter using improvised tools like wood or reeds is defined not by the material itself, but by its ability to sever the windpipe (awdaj). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'ease in necessity' (taysir), allowing common sharp objects to suffice when a dedicated knife is absent, provided the cut is sufficient to ensure proper blood drainage.
